title: Ansel and the Hollow
premise: Edmund Marchetti, a runaway apprentice hiding her magic in the magic-hating city of Vell, discovers that the old gods — long silent since the kingdom of Ansel fell — are answering prayers again, and that every answered prayer burns a hole in the world. The usurper's armies are marching on the free cities, hunting the source: a living door called the Hollow, which only someone carrying Ansel's bloodline can open. Edmund learns her hedge-witch mistress was the last keeper of that bloodline and passed it to her deliberately. To save the free cities she must stop running, claim an inheritance she never wanted, and open the Hollow — knowing it will unmake the country's ghost and take from her the one thing she cannot replace.
about_author: C. M. Quintana is the pen name of a former archivist who grew up between two languages and never quite belonged to either, a displacement that haunts every border-crossing in their fiction. They live quietly with too many maps and write about people who inherit burdens they never asked to carry.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. In outlawed-magic Vell, Edmund sells luck-knots and fever-charms under a false name, three years into hiding from her former mistress, Mother Ilex. When a customer's dying child is healed by a charm Edmund didn't actually enchant, she realizes real power moved through her hands. Emotional beat: dread beneath routine — the past has found her pulse again.

chapters.title: The Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Investigating the healing, Edmund witnesses a street beggar's prayer answered by something vast and old; the spot where it happened is scorched into absence. She recognizes the god's sigil from Mother Ilex's forbidden lessons — an Anselic rite. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear as she understands the gods' return is not mercy but leakage.

chapters.title: What the Mistress Kept
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, with letters from Mother Ilex interleaved. A courier delivers Ilex's posthumous letter: Edmund was chosen not for talent but for blood — she carries the last Anselic line, and the Hollow door answers to it. The usurper's inquisitors are already asking after Ilex's apprentices. Emotional beat: betrayal and grief braided together; her whole exile was designed.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Confer
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, arriving in the free city of Ostra. The city council debates surrender versus resistance while refugees bring rumors of villages erased where prayers were answered. Edmund meets Sefa, a cartographer mapping places that no longer exist, including Ansel itself. Emotional beat: belonging offered for the first time — and immediately threatened.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Road
chapters.summary: POV Corvane, the usurper's god-hunter, marching his armies west. He believes the old gods are a disease and the Hollow a wound to be cauterized; he also carries a private grief the gods refused to answer years ago. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy — the antagonist is a man who prayed once and was abandoned.

chapters.title: Into the Ghost Country
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Guided by Sefa's impossible maps, Edmund crosses into the lingering echo of Ansel, where the fallen kingdom persists as fog, memory, and half-real roads. There she meets the ghost of the last keeper — Mother Ilex's own teacher — who tests her worthiness and shows her what opening the Hollow costs. Emotional beat: temptation; here, at last, is a place she could belong forever.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The ghost-keeper reveals the terms: the Hollow opens once, for everyone, and its keeper must remain inside as its anchor — trading one exile for another, permanent one. Edmund flees the ghost country rather than accept, and finds Ostra burning at its edges. Emotional beat: cowardice confronted; survival has always been her religion, and it fails her now.

chapters.title: Surrender Terms
chapters.summary: POV alternating Edmund/Corvane. Corvane offers the free cities peace if they hand over the Anselic heir. The council wavers; Sefa urges Edmund to run again, and this time means it kindly. Edmund instead sends Corvane a message naming herself — choosing to be hunted so the cities can choose to fight. Emotional beat: the runaway stops running; inheritance claimed on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Hollow Opens
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, climax. At the ruined shrine where Ansel died, Edmund faces Corvane's army and opens the Hollow — not as a weapon but as a door home, letting the ghost-country's exiled dead and displaced living pour through to safety while the old gods finally pass beyond the world, their leaking prayers ended. Corvane, offered passage through, refuses and is left in a world with no more miracles to hate. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured — she gives up escape to give everyone else one.

chapters.title: A Door, Ajar
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, epilogue. Inside the Hollow, Edmund tends a new country built from memory and mercy, visited through the door by Sefa and the free cities' pilgrims. She is no longer apprentice, fugitive, or heir — she is keeper of a place that exists because she chose it. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging was never found, it was made, and survival's price becomes a gift freely paid.
